section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces latent inhibition (LI) and its potential link to both psychosis and creativity, especially in high-IQ individuals. It describes a meta-analysis of two studies, conducted on youthful high-IQ samples, which found that high lifetime creative achievers had significantly lower LI scores than low creative achievers (r = .31). The authors propose that reduced LI, combined with high IQ, may foster creative achievement, distinguishing creative individuals from those with psychosis. The section explicitly refers to 'two studies' and 'two participant samples'.
